Order Instructions

Wholesale Lender Order Instructions:

All communication for “theLender” should be sent to appraisals@thelender.com

 

This lender requires apprasiers to comment and take pictures of ALL CO2 & smoke detectors. This is in their engagement instructions, but they seem to miss it frequently. Please relay this info to the apprasier.

 

Commercial Residential 5-8 Unit Product: All units must be fully inspected. For this loan program, client can accept a 71A, 71B (depending on loan amount), or a commercial narrative report.

5-25 Unit Bridge Product: A minimum inspection of the greater of 3 occupied units or 10% of the total units is required.

2-Unit Commercial Mixed-Use Loan Program: For this program, client can accept either a commercial narrative or a GP appraisal.


Client Order Instructions:

Client Communication Protocol:

They want to be notified only the below:

  1. Extended TT approval needed
  2. Increased fee approval needed
  3. Inspection date, when scheduled
  4. When inspection completed
  5. Any changes to ETA or any concerns on property etc, where we must get them involved etc
  6. If report is late via clients ETA, then yes let them know action being done

The lender has requested a reconsideration for the report due to the following reason:

I reviewed the appraisal for 229 Woodlawn Avenue and would like to request a formal reconsideration of the $154,500 value. I believe approximately $160,000 better reflects the property, and I would appreciate a review of how its features were compared with the selected homes. My concern is whether the vaulted ceilings throughout the living room, custom interior finishes, front porch, and covered outdoor patio received adequate consideration. The report identifies 144 sq. ft. and 420 sq. ft. of covered porch space, yet no porch/patio adjustments were applied to comparable sales #1 and #2. Please explain whether those properties offer equivalent outdoor improvements and how any differences were evaluated. Please also review whether the Q4 quality rating and lack of quality adjustments adequately reflect the differences between my home’s finishes and those of the comparable properties. Additionally, the report’s cost approach indicates $160,180, and comparable #4 has an adjusted value of $158,740. Please explain how these indications were weighed in reaching the final value. I can provide photos and a detailed list of the finishes and improvements to assist with this review. Please have these specific points addressed by the appraiser.
The lender has requested a reconsideration on behalf of the Borrower.
